sutta: then 1.5.8  monks i know not of any other single thing so quick to change as the mind in so much as in so much that it is no easy thing to illustrate how quick to change it is that's all this suta sutra and this is telling us that the mind changes extremely fast and because it changes extremely fast if we know we should use use it to good advantage for example if we have a good result a good intention that comes up for example some people think oh maybe i should become a monk so because there's a good intention you should quickly act if you don't act slowly yeah your mind will change the mind is fickle so when there's a good intention there's a good result we are afraid that it might change we quickly act on the other hand if you have a bad intention or bad  resolve then you should not act on it for example anger rises and then you think you want to you if you react with a lot of anger and definitely you're going to do something which is unwholesome which is not wise because your state of mind is troubled and once you know that now then instead of acting you don't do anything just wait wait for the anger to subside and because the mind is quick to change it will subside if you just keep on waiting just do nothing just resolve not to act on it so that is using this with wisdom the fact that the mind can change very fast the buddha said this mind monks is luminous but it is defiled by things that come from without
